https://www.koreatimes.co.kr/world/20261.body: SEATTLE — Democrats' sweeping victories in Tuesday's U.S. midterm elections brought relief to many Koreans frustrated with President Donald Trump, but that relief did not necessarily translate into support for the Democratic Party. That was how Bo Young Lee, a Korean American business executive, summed up the election results. "Ultimately, the results on Tuesday were a byproduct of citizens' frustration with the Trump administration, rising costs, and the attacks on democracy," Lee, an international speaker specializing in AI ethics and corporate diversity, told The Korea Times. Another Korean American voter, a 47-year-old Texas resident who has traditionally supported Republicans, said she crossed party lines for the first time in Tuesday's election. "I voted Democratic simply because I wanted anyone but the Republicans," she said, requesting anonymity. "It was the first time in my life I'd ever voted for a Democrat." Her decision came as Texas, long considered a Republican stronghold, delivered some of the election's biggest surprises. Democrats won the governorship and a U.S. Senate seat in the state for the first time in decades, marking a dramatic shift in a state that had consistently rejected Democratic candidates in statewide races. The Democratic victories dealt a major setback to Trump, giving the party control of both chambers of Congress and setting the stage for a divided government during the remaining two years of his presidency. Across Korean-language online communities, the results prompted everything from celebrations to expressions of disbelief and cautious optimism. "I've lived in the U.S. for 20 years, and this is the first time I've paid so much attention to a midterm election," one commenter wrote. "I thought America had no hope after Trump became president for a second time. Now I feel a little reassured. At least there will be some checks on Trump's unchecked power." Another commenter said the results brought tears, describing the comfort of realizing that many others shared the same frustrations. Yet the conversations also showed that opposition to Trump did not necessarily translate into support for Democrats. One California resident said they had traditionally voted Republican because of disagreements with Democratic policies but voted Democratic this time out of frustration with Trump. "I absolutely despise Trump, but I don't support Democrats either because I disagree with many of their policies," one person wrote. Much of the debate centered on everyday concerns rather than party loyalty. Some blamed Trump's tariffs and economic policies for worsening the cost of living. Others worried that Democratic policies would increase government spending and place greater burdens on middle-class families. Education also emerged as a contentious issue, particularly among parents discussing LGBTQ-related topics in schools. Some expressed concerns about what their children were being taught, while others pushed back against what they considered exaggerated fears. The contrasting views highlighted differing political views among Korean Americans, with some putting aside longstanding party loyalties to oppose Trump while others remained skeptical of Democratic policies. Lee said the results reflected broader dissatisfaction with the Trump administration, but warned that Democrats should not take their victories for granted. "The newly elected Democrats can't forget the frustration that swept them into office. If people don't see meaningful change within a short period, we may see different results in 2028," she said
https://www.koreatimes.co.kr/world/20261.title_zh: 旅美韩国人欢迎民主党取得胜利，但对未来走向仍存疑虑
https://www.koreatimes.co.kr/world/20261.body_zh: 西雅图——民主党在周二举行的美国中期选举中取得压倒性胜利，这让许多对唐纳德·特朗普总统感到失望的韩国人如释重负，但这种宽慰未必转化为对民主党的支持。旅美韩裔企业高管Bo Young Lee正是这样总结此次选举结果的。李在接受《韩国时报》采访时说：“归根结底，周二的结果是公民对特朗普政府的不满、生活成本上涨以及针对民主制度的攻击共同造成的副产品。”李是一名专注于人工智能伦理和企业多元化的国际演讲者。另一名旅美韩裔选民是一名47岁的得克萨斯州居民，过去一直支持共和党；她说，周二这次选举是她首次跨党派投票。“我投票给民主党，只是因为除了共和党之外，我愿意支持任何人。”她表示，并要求匿名。“这是我有生以来第一次投票给民主党人。”她的决定出现在得克萨斯州出人意料的选举结果之中。长期以来，得克萨斯州一直被视为共和党的大本营，但在此次选举中，民主党数十年来首次赢得该州州长职位和一个美国联邦参议院席位，这在该州全州范围的选举中历来拒绝民主党候选人的背景下，标志着一场剧烈转变。民主党的胜利对特朗普构成重大打击，使该党掌控了国会两院，并为特朗普剩余两年任期内的分立政府局面铺路。在韩语网络社群中，选举结果引发了庆祝、难以置信和谨慎乐观等不同反应。一名评论者写道：“我在美国生活了20年，这是第一次如此关注中期选举。我原以为特朗普第二任期开始后，美国就毫无希望了。现在我感到稍微安心了一些。至少会对特朗普不受制约的权力形成一些制衡。”另一名评论者说，选举结果令她感动落泪，因为意识到许多人也怀着同样的不满。然而，讨论也表明，反特朗普并不一定会转化为支持民主党。一名加利福尼亚州居民说，由于与民主党政策存在分歧，他过去一直投票给共和党，但此次出于对特朗普的不满而投票给民主党。一人写道：“我非常厌恶特朗普，但也不支持民主党，因为他们许多政策都与我相左。”争论大多围绕日常生活问题，而非党派忠诚。一些人将生活成本恶化归咎于特朗普的关税和经济政策。另一些人担心，民主党的政策会增加政府支出，给中产家庭带来更沉重的负担。教育也成为一个有争议的话题，尤其是在讨论学校 LGBTQ相关议题的家长之中。一些人担忧孩子正在接受的教育内容，另一些人则反驳他们认为被夸大的恐惧。这些对立观点凸显了韩裔美国人之间不同的政治立场：一些人搁置长期以来的党派忠诚，以反对特朗普；另一些人则仍对民主党政策持怀疑态度。李表示，选举结果反映了人们对特朗普政府更广泛的不满，但警告民主党不应把胜利视为理所当然。她说：“新当选的民主党人不能忘记，正是这股不满情绪把他们推上了台。如果人们短期内看不到有意义的改变，那么2028年我们可能会看到不同的结果。”
